item.title: Akita Events 2026: Kanto Festival, Omagari Fireworks & Namahage
item.description: Akita’s calendar swings between two extremes: a summer of luminous festivals and Japan’s most prestigious fireworks, and a deep winter of snow igloos and demon rituals. The Kanto Festival’s forests of balanced lantern-poles are one of Tohoku’s three great summer festivals; the Omagari competition is where Japan’s top pyrotechnicians battle for the national crown; and in February, the Oga Peninsula’s Namahage demons and Yokote’s candle-lit snow huts define northern winter. This guide gathers the events worth planning a 2026 trip around, with a month-by-month calendar at the end.

item.title: Omagari Fireworks Championship: Japan's Top Pyrotechnics — Guide
item.description: Japan’s most prestigious fireworks competition — held in Daisen (formerly Omagari) on the last Saturday of August, this century-old competition draws 30 pyrotechnic teams from across Japan to display their finest original creations. Over 18,000 shells light up the night sky above the Omono River before some 800,000 spectators, judged for artistry as much as scale. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Daisen, Akita Hours Evening, last Saturday of August Admission Free viewing; paid seats sell out early Time needed 3 hours Best time Last Saturday of August (fixed) Highlights 30 pyrotechnic teams competing nationally.
